name: Balantioides coli

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Trophozoite: approximately 40–200 µm, with surface cilia, a cytostome and kidney-shaped macronucleus.
Cyst: roughly 50–70 µm, rounded with a thick wall; internal nuclear detail may be less apparent.

transmission.detail: Ingested cysts excyst and trophozoites colonize the large intestine; some invade mucosa, and encystation precedes shedding.

life_cycle.detail: Ingested cysts excyst and trophozoites colonize the large intestine; some invade mucosa, and encystation precedes shedding.

hosts: Pigs are major reservoirs; humans and other mammals may be infected. No intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide, especially where pig-associated fecal contamination occurs.
clinical_significance: May be asymptomatic or cause colitis, diarrhea and dysentery.
diagnostics: Fresh wet mounts at 100–400× demonstrate large, ciliated motile trophozoites; permanent preparations support morphology.
differential_diagnosis: Large size and cilia distinguish trophozoites from amoebae; cysts need wall and internal-feature assessment, not size alone.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Balantioides coli — Large intestinal ciliate. May be asymptomatic or cause colitis, diarrhea and dysentery.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
